_comment: Canonical response wire format. This is the exact JSON shape received after invoking a Brique capacity. All _note fields are documentation-only.
_intention_id_note: Echoes the intention_id of the intention that produced this response. Use it to correlate responses to their originating intention.

to._comment: The original caller address (echoed from intention.from).

from._comment: The capacity that produced this response.

identity._comment: Internal runtime identity only. External authentication is carried by the signed transport envelope and must never be embedded here.

_status_note: Required. 'ok' or 'error' is the FINAL answer of the intention: exactly one of them comes back. 'running' is an intermediate answer, not final: a capacity that works for a long time says so zero, one or many times (the wrapper libraries' notify_running or keepalive), with the same intention_id and no payload, and its final 'ok' or 'error' follows. A caller that awaits an answer keeps waiting on 'running' (it also renews the silence budget of a call to a peer instance) and never treats it as the result. Check this field first before reading payload or error.

payload._comment: Present when status='ok'. Shape is capacity-specific — see the capacity descriptor outputs.payload for the exact fields. Absent or null when status='error'.

error._comment: Present only when status='error'. Absent when status='ok'.
error._origin_note: The engine family that produced the error. Accepted values: 'communication', 'execution', 'matter', 'trace', 'reflexive', 'control', 'user', 'wrapper'.
error._code_note: Accepted values: 'refused' (capacity declined the request), 'invalid' (bad params or shape), 'not_found' (addressed resource does not exist), 'unauthorized' (identity or permission failure), 'conflict' (state conflict, e.g. revision mismatch), 'timeout' (execution exceeded allowed time), 'unavailable' (dependency or resource not available), 'canceled' (intentionally stopped), 'internal' (unexpected engine error), 'configuration' (misconfigured descriptor or engine), 'read_fail' (read operation failed).

details._comment: Optional. Free-form key-value pairs providing structured error context. Common keys: 'reason' (short machine-readable cause string).
details._reason_note: Some stable reasons, among others, with what to do. REFUSED BEFORE ANY EFFECT, safe to send again after a pause: 'loop busy' or 'busy' (the family or wrapper had no free place), 'rate_limited' (the heavy-operation rate of the caller is spent), 'byte_budget_exceeded' (the Matter byte budget of the caller is spent and refills over time). REFUSED, change the request: 'payload_too_large' (over the message size limit; move big content through a Matter substance lease), 'response_too_large' (the answer does not fit the browser bridge: ask for less, a shorter range or fewer nodes), 'quota_reached' (too many leases or transfers), 'disk_space_low' (the instance is under min_free_disk_mib and refuses every Matter write), 'revision_mismatch' (the element changed since it was read: read it again, then retry), 'wrapper_not_configured' (the wrapper is not declared in this capacity's own context). OUTCOME UNKNOWN, the call may have run: 'connection_lost' (the connection of the call went away), 'timeout_waiting_answer', 'context_stopped', 'context_unreachable'. SECURITY: for an external caller (a restricted local principal, a peer, a browser) an element it may not touch is indistinguishable from one that does not exist: code 'not_found' with reason 'not_found'; a capacity it is not granted answers code 'unauthorized', reason 'capability_denied', message 'not authorized'. The rule that refused it is only in the denial journal of the instance (brique-sec denials), never in the response.

_reading_a_response._comment: Decision tree for reading a response.
_reading_a_response.step_1: Check status. 'running' is not an answer: keep waiting for the final one. If 'error', read error.code, error.details.reason and error.message, and do not repeat the call before understanding why: an error whose reason says the outcome is unknown may already have had effects. Do not read payload.
_reading_a_response.step_2: If status='ok', read payload fields as declared in the capacity descriptor outputs.payload.
_reading_a_response.step_3: Some payload fields are conditionally present (e.g. data in matter.read only when 'data' was in read_mode). Check the capacity descriptor invariants and success conditions.

_ok_response_example._comment: A successful matter.read response with inline data.
